pillar_reactions.evidence: 'Yeah, perfect.' When the rep pushed for what made it perfect, the answer was specific: 'The whole thing that I can go with the coach from step by step.' Understood and agreed with no objection.

'Okay, good.' The rep noticed the flatness and probed — 'Well, what's good about it? doesn't sound that certain.' — and got 'I don't know how to say, what to say more. I'm just listening to you, trying to remember the information you say.' No objection, but no engagement either; he was taking notes rather than reacting.

The only pillar he volunteered a positive reaction to and the one he singled out: 'The third one, one-on-one coaching is more interesting for me because I have, I never had the experience like this. Because all the time when I go to the gym, I used to work for myself by my own way, from information that I get from YouTube, from Instagram.' He then defined what he wanted from it in his own words — not motivation but correction: 'today I want to eat some chocolate cookie bar, for example. And I told this for my coach, and he told me, no, Farid, today, it's not a good choice.'

anchors.raw: I can tell you that this process is like for US citizens, maybe for Europe citizens, it will be a little bit more than for average prices of the trainers, for example, in my city, but it's okay, I know the market, it's okay.
anchors.note: He explicitly compared the offer against his local market, concluded it was above it, and accepted it anyway on the basis that the product is different. This is the only prospect in the batch who priced the offer against a competitor and still endorsed it. It also confirms that the Latvian market rate is materially below the US rate, which matters for any European expansion.

anchors.raw: Well, no, it's okay for six months. It's a 1K month average price. So for one-on-one coaching, when I every time be on touch with my coach, so I think that it's okay. It's a good price.
anchors.note: Every prospect in this batch converted $6,000 into $1,000/month within seconds. He is the only one for whom the conversion supported the price rather than undermined it, because he valued unlimited coach access at that rate. Worth noting that the reps do not present the monthly figure — the prospects compute it themselves, every time.

anchors.raw: We have an investment of 6K dollars, which I think is around 5K euros.
anchors.note: Rep-initiated conversion for a eurozone prospect. It lands the price in the buyer's own currency and lowers the headline number, and the prospect accepted it without querying the rate.

unmet_demand.want: A written summary of the programme and terms to review before committing $6,000
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Asked for directly and answered with an admission that no such document exists: 'I'll send a few things over to you on WhatsApp. There's nothing like specific that I have like in paper written.' For a prospect whose entire stated decision process is offline analysis, the absence of a leave-behind is the specific thing standing between a 9/10 and a signature.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that the nutrition protocol will survive frequent travel
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This was his stated reason for a 9 rather than a 10 — 'I'm addicted to traveling. I'm a travel guy. So I just think that maybe sometimes it would be difficult for me to do some work to keep my nutrition.' The rep answered it reasonably by contrasting a protocol with a fixed meal plan, and the prospect accepted, but nothing concrete was offered.
